items.title: Joel Dorn interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2007
items.q: I go into the office, right, and this guy I work with Mark Schulman, he said, “Clint Eastwood’s on the phone for you.”

ctx.x: Simple. The arranger hired him. I never met Bucky. Let me tell you about that first record. Rahsaan had called me up from Washington and he said, “I’ve got a girl singer for you.” I said, “what’s her name?” He said, “Roberta Novosel, she’s married to my bass player, Steve Novosel.” I said okay. And I said to him, “what does she sound like?” And he got mad and he said, “she sounds like a colored lady” and he slammed the phone down, you know? I don’t know what I said, you know, what does she sound like? About a…

done with the second record and I get a phone call one morning. I go into the office, right, and this guy I work with Mark Schulman, he said, “Clint Eastwood’s on the phone for you.” So I thought it was like somebody goofing, right? So I get on the phone and I go, “hello, Clint?” and he goes, “yes.” I said, “listen I can’t really talk to you right now, I’ve got Winston Churchill on the other phone, can you call back later?”
